title: Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II - Probe Connector Damage or Probe Not Recognized
description: Guide for troubleshooting probe recognition issues and possible connector damage on a Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II ultrasound system.

steps.title: Power Cycle the System
steps.instructions: Turn off the Edge II and unplug AC power if connected. Wait 30–60 seconds, then restart the system. Reason: Resets internal communication between the system and probe.

steps.title: Inspect the Probe Connector and Cable
steps.instructions: Check for bent pins, debris, corrosion, or visible damage on the probe connector. Inspect the probe cable for cuts, fraying, or kinks. Reason: Physical damage can prevent proper connection and recognition.

steps.title: Clean the Connector Contacts
steps.instructions: Use a lint-free cloth or approved isopropyl alcohol wipe on the probe connector and system port. Ensure the system is powered off during cleaning. Reason: Dirt or residue can block proper electrical contact.

steps.title: Reconnect the Probe Firmly
steps.instructions: Insert the probe fully into the system port until it clicks or seats properly. Avoid twisting or forcing the connector. Reason: Loose connections are a common cause of 'not detected' errors.

steps.title: Test with Another Compatible Probe
steps.instructions: If available, connect a different, known-working probe to the same port. If the new probe is recognized, the original probe is likely faulty. Reason: Isolates whether the issue is the probe or the system connector.

steps.title: Test the Suspect Probe on Another Edge II Unit
steps.instructions: If another Edge II is available, connect the probe there. If it fails on multiple systems, the probe itself is likely defective.

CCR.Complaint: Probe not detected on the Edge II.
CCR.Cause: Probe connector showed bent pins and intermittent contact; system did not recognize probe.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned connector, tested with another probe, confirmed original probe faulty; labeled probe Out of Service and sent for repair.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II - Image Artifacts or Degraded Image Quality
description: Guide to troubleshoot image artifacts or degraded quality on Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II ultrasound systems, focusing on external causes first.

steps.title: Verify Probe Connection
steps.instructions: Ensure the probe is fully seated in the connector. Loose or partially connected probes can cause artifacts. Inspect the connector for bent pins or debris.

steps.title: Swap or Inspect the Probe
steps.instructions: Test with a known-good probe to see if the artifact persists. If the image improves, the original probe may be damaged.

steps.title: Check the Cable and Strain Relief
steps.instructions: Examine the probe cable for kinks, cuts, or frayed areas. Damaged cables can cause intermittent signal loss.

steps.title: Review System Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm presets and imaging modes are correct for the intended study. Reset the image settings to default to rule out incorrect gain, depth, or frequency settings.

steps.title: Check the Display and Monitor Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect video output cables and monitor connections for loose connections or damage. Confirm the display itself is functioning correctly by swapping monitors if available.

steps.title: Power Cycle the System
steps.instructions: Turn the system off, wait 30–60 seconds, then restart. This can resolve temporary software glitches affecting image processing.

steps.title: Run Built-in Self-Test / Diagnostic Tools
steps.instructions: Utilize the Edge II’s internal diagnostics to check for probe or system errors. Document any error codes for escalation.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound images appear grainy and show streaking artifacts during exams.
CCR.Cause: Probe was properly seated but the same artifact persisted on multiple probes; system presets verified; cables and display connections intact.
CCR.Resolution: System removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for bench evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Final device status: Out of Service

title: Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II - Battery Charging Issues
description: Troubleshooting guide for battery charging issues on the Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II ultrasound system, focusing on external checks before internal failure.

steps.title: Verify AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Ensure the system is plugged into a known working outlet. Test the outlet with another device or a voltmeter. Reason: A faulty outlet or power strip is a common cause of battery not charging.

steps.title: Check Power Cord and Adapter
steps.instructions: Inspect the power cord for cuts, frays, or bent connectors. Confirm the AC adapter matches the specifications for the Edge II. Swap with a known-good cord/adapter if available. Reason: Damaged cords or incorrect adapters prevent proper charging.

steps.title: Confirm Battery Seating
steps.instructions: Remove and reseat the battery in the device. Ensure the battery clicks fully into place and terminals align correctly. Reason: Poor contact can prevent charging or cause intermittent detection.

steps.title: Inspect Battery for Damage
steps.instructions: Look for swelling, leaks, corrosion, or unusual heat. Reason: Physical damage indicates the battery should be removed from service.

steps.title: Observe System Indicators
steps.instructions: Check the on-screen battery icon or LEDs. Note any error codes or messages displayed when connected to AC. Reason: System diagnostics may identify whether the issue is the battery or device circuitry.

steps.title: Test with a Known-Good Battery
steps.instructions: If available, insert a different, fully charged Edge II battery. Observe if it charges normally. Reason: Confirms whether the issue is with the battery or the system.

steps.title: Power Cycle the System
steps.instructions: Shut down the ultrasound, remove AC power and battery, wait 1–2 minutes, then reconnect and power on. Reason: Resets charging circuitry and clears minor firmware glitches.

CCR.Complaint: Battery not charging, system only works on AC power.
CCR.Cause: Observed that the AC outlet and adapter are functioning, battery seated correctly, but the system does not charge. Battery indicator remains static.
CCR.Resolution: Removed device from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for repair evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Battery inspected: Yes, no visible damage
Error messages observed: None or specific battery alert
Final device status: Out of Service

title: Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II - Buttons or Keypad Failure
description: Guide to troubleshoot unresponsive or malfunctioning buttons and keypad on Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II ultrasound system.

steps.title: Confirm System Power
steps.instructions: Ensure the ultrasound system is powered on and the battery has sufficient charge or the unit is connected to AC power. Why: A low battery or unstable power can cause input lag or unresponsive keys.

steps.title: Visual Inspection of Keypad
steps.instructions: Check for visible debris, liquid contamination, or damage around keys. Why: Dirt, dust, or spills can prevent proper key contact.

steps.title: Clean the Keypad
steps.instructions: Use a lint-free cloth lightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol to clean around and on the keys. Avoid excessive liquid. Why: Cleaning removes dirt and oils that may block electrical contact.

steps.title: Check for External Key Lock or Function Mode
steps.instructions: Verify that any “lock” or “function mode” settings on the system are not engaged (refer to system touchscreen menus). Why: Some ultrasound systems allow locking buttons to prevent accidental presses.

steps.title: Test All Keys Methodically
steps.instructions: Press each button or key individually while observing system response. Note any keys that are non-responsive or inconsistent. Why: Pinpoints which buttons are failing and helps rule out software vs. hardware issues.

steps.title: Restart the System
steps.instructions: Perform a controlled system reboot. Why: Sometimes software glitches can temporarily disable keypad input.

steps.title: Check for Firmware Updates
steps.instructions: Ensure the device firmware is current per manufacturer guidance. Why: Firmware updates can resolve known input or keypad issues.

CCR.Complaint: Several keys on the Edge II keypad do not respond, and imaging cannot be fully controlled.
CCR.Cause: External inspection revealed no liquid damage. Keypad cleaning and system restart did not restore functionality. Likely internal keypad failure.
CCR.Resolution: Device removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for vendor repair.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II - System Boot or Software Errors
description: Guide for troubleshooting boot failures, startup errors, and software crashes on the Fujifilm Sonosite Edge II ultrasound system.

steps.title: Verify Power Source
steps.instructions: Ensure the system is plugged into a known working outlet. Check power cords and connections for damage or looseness. Confirm that the AC power indicator is on. Why it matters: Many “boot failures” are actually due to unstable or missing power.

steps.title: Check Battery Condition
steps.instructions: If running on battery, connect AC power and observe LED indicators. Swap with a known good battery if available. Why it matters: Weak or depleted batteries can prevent proper boot.

steps.title: Inspect External Cables and Peripherals
steps.instructions: Disconnect all probes, USB devices, and network cables. Attempt boot with minimal configuration. Why it matters: Faulty peripherals can halt software initialization.

steps.title: Soft Reset / Safe Boot (if available)
steps.instructions: Follow manufacturer’s procedure to perform a soft reset or safe boot mode. Observe any error messages displayed. Why it matters: Safe boot may allow the system to bypass minor software issues.

steps.title: Check for Visible Damage or Overheating
steps.instructions: Inspect for unusual heat, burning smell, or liquid damage. Ensure vents are clear and fan is functional. Why it matters: Overheating or physical damage can prevent proper startup.

steps.title: Observe Error Codes
steps.instructions: Document any messages or codes that appear on startup. Refer to manufacturer support resources for error code meanings.

CCR.Complaint: Edge II will not boot and shows ‘Software Error 101’ on startup.
CCR.Cause: Power confirmed stable, battery verified, no external peripherals attached, soft reset failed; system still displays error.
CCR.Resolution: System removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent to the repair bench for evaluation.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite X-Porte Ultrasound System - Probe Not Recognized or Connection Errors
description: Troubleshooting probe detection issues, intermittent connections, or transducer errors caused by connection problems, port faults, or probe failure.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the probe from patient use and transition imaging to another ultrasound system if needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Connect the probe and power on the system. Confirm the probe is not recognized or an error message is displayed.

steps.title: Inspect the Probe Connector and Cable
steps.instructions: Check for bent or missing pins, dirt, gel, or debris, cracked housing or worn cable strain relief. Clean using approved methods if needed.

steps.title: Reseat the Probe Connection
steps.instructions: Disconnect and firmly reconnect the probe to the X-Porte port. Ensure it is fully inserted and secured.

steps.title: Test with a Known Working Probe
steps.instructions: Connect a different probe that is known to be functional. Second probe works → original probe is faulty. Second probe fails → system or port issue likely.

steps.title: Test the Suspect Probe on Another Compatible System
steps.instructions: If available, test the probe on another Sonosite system. Works elsewhere → X-Porte issue. Fails again → probe failure confirmed.

steps.title: Inspect the Probe Port on the X-Porte
steps.instructions: Visually inspect the port for bent or recessed pins, debris or contamination, and physical damage. Do not insert objects into the port.

steps.title: Restart the System
steps.instructions: Power down the X-Porte completely, wait 30 seconds, then restart.

steps.title: Check System Software Behavior
steps.instructions: Observe for additional system errors or abnormal behavior. Ensure the system is not frozen or partially responsive.

CCR.Complaint: Probe not recognized on Sonosite X-Porte ultrasound system.
CCR.Cause: Faulty probe with damaged connector pins.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced probe and confirmed proper recognition and imaging.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite X-Porte Ultrasound System - Image Artifact or Quality Degradation
description: Troubleshooting image artifacts, poor resolution, shadowing, or inconsistent image quality caused by probes, settings, or external factors.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: If image quality is impacting diagnosis, remove the system from patient use and move the patient to a known working ultrasound system. Diagnostic accuracy is critical, and poor imaging can lead to clinical risk.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the system and reproduce the issue. Observe the image for lines, dropouts, or streaks, grainy or low-resolution image, and uneven brightness or shadowing. Expected: Artifact or degradation is visible and repeatable. Why it matters: Confirms a real system issue versus user perception or setup.

steps.title: Check Probe Condition and Cleanliness
steps.instructions: Inspect the probe for cracks in the lens, delamination or bubbling, and residue, gel buildup, or debris. Clean the probe using approved methods. Expected: Probe surface is clean and intact. Why it matters: Probe damage or contamination is the most common cause of image artifacts.

steps.title: Test with a Known Good Probe
steps.instructions: Swap the probe with another compatible, known working probe. Expected: If image improves → original probe is faulty. If issue persists → problem is system-related. Why it matters: Quickly isolates probe vs system fault.

steps.title: Inspect Probe Connection and Port
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the probe firmly. Inspect connector for bent or damaged pins and debris or fluid intrusion. Try a different probe port if available. Expected: Secure connection with no visible damage. Why it matters: Poor connections can cause signal loss and artifacts.

steps.title: Check Imaging Settings
steps.instructions: Verify settings such as gain and depth, frequency selection, and preset (correct exam type selected). Reset to a default preset if needed. Expected: Image improves with proper settings. Why it matters: Incorrect configuration can mimic hardware issues.

steps.title: Evaluate Environmental and External Factors
steps.instructions: Check for excessive gel or air gaps, poor probe contact with patient, and electrical interference from nearby equipment. Expected: Stable image when conditions are optimized. Why it matters: External factors can introduce artifacts without device failure.

steps.title: Reboot the System
steps.instructions: Perform a full system restart. Expected: Temporary software-related artifacts may clear. Why it matters: Clears minor software or processing faults.

steps.title: Check for Overheating or System Warnings
steps.instructions: Ensure ventilation is not blocked and system is not overheating. Listen for abnormal fan behavior. Expected: System operates within normal temperature range. Why it matters: Thermal issues can degrade imaging performance.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound image appears grainy with intermittent lines during scanning.
CCR.Cause: Defective probe identified after testing with a known good probe resolved the issue.
CCR.Resolution: Removed faulty probe from service and replaced with functional probe; system returned to service.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite X-Porte Ultrasound System - System Fails to Boot or Software Errors
description: Troubleshooting system boot failures, startup freezes, or software errors caused by power, peripherals, or internal issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the system from active patient use. If in use, transfer imaging needs to another ultrasound system before proceeding.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to power on the system and observe for no power, boot screen freeze, error messages, or repeated restarts.

steps.title: Check Power Source and External Connections
steps.instructions: Verify outlet functionality, ensure power cable is securely connected, and check for power indicator lights.

steps.title: Inspect for Battery-Related Issues
steps.instructions: Attempt to power on using battery only, then reconnect AC power and observe charging indicators.

steps.title: Disconnect All External Accessories
steps.instructions: Remove probes and all peripherals, then power cycle and attempt startup again.

steps.title: Perform a Full Power Cycle
steps.instructions: Power off, unplug from AC, wait 60–90 seconds, reconnect power, and restart the system.

steps.title: Check for Overheating or Environmental Factors
steps.instructions: Ensure vents are clear, listen for fan operation, and check for excessive heat.

steps.title: Observe Error Messages or Codes
steps.instructions: Document exact wording of any errors and note when they occur during startup.

steps.title: Attempt Alternate Startup (If Applicable)
steps.instructions: Retry startup multiple times and observe consistency of failure point.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound system will not boot and displays software error during startup.
CCR.Cause: System failed to complete boot process after removal of external accessories, indicating likely internal software or hardware fault.
CCR.Resolution: System removed from service, labeled Out of Service, and sent for vendor repair evaluation.

helpfulDetails: Any error messages or codes displayed

title: Fujifilm Sonosite X-Porte Ultrasound System - DICOM or Network Export Failure
description: Troubleshooting failed image export, PACS communication issues, and network-related DICOM failures.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot during active patient use. Move to a backup system if imaging/export is urgently needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt export to PACS and note errors such as timeouts, rejection, or no response.

steps.title: Check Network Connection (Physical Layer)
steps.instructions: Inspect Ethernet cable, verify link lights, and test with a known working cable and port.

steps.title: Verify Network Connectivity on the System
steps.instructions: Confirm valid IP, subnet, and gateway. Ensure IP is not 0.0.0.0 or 169.254.x.x and reboot if needed.

steps.title: Test Network Availability
steps.instructions: Use ping or connectivity tools or confirm port activity with IT.

steps.title: Verify DICOM Configuration
steps.instructions: Ensure AE Title, IP, and port match PACS configuration exactly.

steps.title: Check for Recent Changes
steps.instructions: Identify recent network, PACS, or location changes that may affect connectivity.

steps.title: Attempt Alternate Export Method
steps.instructions: Test export to USB or alternate DICOM destination to isolate issue.

steps.title: Reboot the System
steps.instructions: Perform full shutdown and restart to clear temporary network or software faults.

CCR.Complaint: Ultrasound unable to send images to PACS; export attempts failing.
CCR.Cause: Incorrect DICOM destination IP configuration after network port change.
CCR.Resolution: Updated DICOM settings to correct PACS IP and verified successful image transmission.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (operational or removed from service)

title: Fujifilm Sonosite X-Porte Ultrasound System - Touchscreen or Control Panel Unresponsive
description: Addresses unresponsive touchscreen or controls due to power, lock settings, external devices, or temporary system/software issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the system from active patient use before troubleshooting. If in use, transfer imaging to another ultrasound system. Why it matters: Prevents interruption of patient care and avoids delays during procedures.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to use both the touchscreen and any physical controls (trackball, buttons). Observe if the entire screen is unresponsive, only certain areas do not respond, or physical controls still work. Expected: Confirm whether the issue is total or partial. Why it matters: Helps differentiate between touchscreen failure and broader system issues.

steps.title: Check for Screen Lock or Software Freeze
steps.instructions: Look for any screen lock icons or inactive UI indicators. Attempt a soft reset by pressing the power button briefly (sleep/wake). Expected: Screen resumes normal responsiveness. Why it matters: Systems can appear frozen due to software lock states.

steps.title: Perform a Full System Reboot
steps.instructions: Power down the system completely. Wait 30–60 seconds, then restart. Expected: Touchscreen and controls respond normally after reboot. Why it matters: Clears temporary software or UI processing errors.

steps.title: Inspect for External Interference or Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect any external USB devices (keyboard, mouse, storage devices). Check for gel, fluid, or debris on the screen or control panel. Clean if needed per manufacturer guidelines. Expected: No obstruction or interference affecting input. Why it matters: External devices or contamination can interfere with touch input.

steps.title: Check Power Stability
steps.instructions: Ensure the system is connected to a reliable power source or has adequate battery charge. Observe for any system lag, flickering, or instability. Expected: Stable power with normal system performance. Why it matters: Low voltage or unstable power can affect system responsiveness.

steps.title: Test Control Panel Functionality
steps.instructions: Use alternate input methods (trackball, keyboard if available). Determine if only the touchscreen is affected. Expected: Other controls function normally if issue is isolated. Why it matters: Helps isolate touchscreen hardware vs full system failure.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Check the touchscreen and control panel for cracks, impact damage, or signs of wear. Expected: No visible damage. Why it matters: Physical damage can cause loss of responsiveness.

CCR.Complaint: Touchscreen and control panel not responding during imaging use.
CCR.Cause: System software freeze causing loss of touchscreen input.
CCR.Resolution: Performed full system reboot; functionality restored and verified normal operation.

helpfulDetails: Any lag, freezing, or error messages
Final device status (working or removed from service)

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Battery Not Charging or Short Runtime
description: Troubleshoots charging failure or reduced battery runtime caused by AC power, battery seating, battery condition, connections, or operating environment.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care Before Battery Testing
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot an unreliable battery while the SonoSite PX is supporting a procedure where unexpected shutdown could affect patient care. Connect to reliable AC power when appropriate or provide another verified ultrasound system before testing. Expected outcome: Clinical care is not dependent on a system with uncertain battery operation.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Battery Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported condition is: Battery does not charge Charging indication is absent Battery percentage does not increase Battery drains unusually quickly System operates only on AC System shuts down when disconnected from AC Complaint affects one battery or all installed batteries Expected outcome: The charging or runtime problem is clearly defined and can be reproduced or objectively evaluated.

steps.title: 3. Verify the AC Power Source
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is connected to a verified working receptacle and that accessible power connections are secure. If used with a powered cart or dock, verify the external cart/dock power path is properly connected. Expected outcome: Reliable AC power is available to the system. If charging resumes after correcting the external power source, the issue is resolved after verification.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Battery and Battery Area
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible battery components for: Swelling Cracked housing Contamination Damaged contacts Loose seating Evidence of overheating Do not continue charging or using a visibly damaged or swollen battery. Expected outcome: The battery is physically safe and correctly installed. Unsafe batteries are removed from service according to facility battery-handling procedures.

steps.title: 5. Reseat Accessible Battery Components
steps.instructions: With the system safely shut down as appropriate, remove and reinstall only batteries designed for normal external access. Confirm they latch or seat fully. Expected outcome: The system recognizes the battery and normal charging indication returns. If reseating corrects the issue, complete runtime and charging verification before returning the system to service.

steps.title: 6. Observe Charge Status Over Time
steps.instructions: Connect the system to verified AC power and observe the battery status. Determine whether the indicated charge level increases rather than relying solely on the presence of a charging symbol. Expected outcome: Charge status progresses normally. If charge indication is present but capacity does not increase, continue troubleshooting.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Compatible Battery
steps.instructions: If an approved known-good compatible battery is available, substitute it without changing internal components. Compare: Battery recognition Charging behavior Ability to operate away from AC Runtime trend under similar operating conditions Expected outcome: A known-good battery operates normally. If it does, the original battery is the likely service item and may be replaced according to approved procedures.

steps.title: 8. Consider Operating Load and Environment
steps.instructions: Confirm that the reported short runtime is not being influenced by obvious operating conditions such as: High display brightness Extensive peripheral use Continuous heavy imaging workflow Battery starting from a partial charge Very hot or cold storage or operating conditions Do not change clinical configuration solely to mask a deteriorated battery. Expected outcome: Runtime concerns are evaluated under a reasonable and repeatable operating condition.

steps.title: 9. Verify Operation on AC and Battery
steps.instructions: Once charging has occurred: Confirm stable operation on AC Disconnect AC under controlled conditions Confirm continued operation on battery Observe battery status for unexpected rapid decline or shutdown Expected outcome: The system transitions between AC and battery operation without interruption and battery status behaves consistently.

steps.title: 10. Complete Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After battery correction or replacement: Verify normal startup Confirm battery recognition Confirm charging indication Confirm basic ultrasound imaging Verify operation away from AC Check for unexpected shutdowns or battery warnings Expected outcome: Charging and battery operation are reliable. Troubleshooting can stop when battery performance is acceptable under the facility's approved verification method.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SonoSite PX battery discharged rapidly and would not support normal mobile use.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found one installed battery had poor runtime while a known-good compatible battery operated and charged normally.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the affected battery, verified charging and battery-powered operation, completed basic imaging checks, and returned the system to service.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Cart, Dock, or External Monitor Communication Failure
description: Troubleshoots cart, docking, or external display problems caused by power, cabling, seating, input selection, connections, or accessory configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care
steps.instructions: If the cart, dock, or external display failure interferes with safe visualization, mobility, power, or use during a procedure, move the patient workflow to another verified ultrasound configuration. Do not troubleshoot unstable physical mounting or damaged cables while the system is being used for patient care. Expected outcome: Clinical care continues without reliance on an unreliable accessory or display path.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which External Component Is Affected
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Cart power or accessory operation Docking connection External monitor Intermittent display No external video Communication lost when the system is moved Accessory recognized only when connected a certain way Multiple cart/dock functions Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to the external monitor, cart, dock, cable, or system connection.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Cart and Dock Physically
steps.instructions: Inspect for: Loose system mounting Damaged dock connectors Bent accessible contacts Debris or contamination Broken latches Pinched cables Damaged strain reliefs Signs of liquid intrusion or impact Do not continue using a cart or dock that cannot safely support or secure the ultrasound system. Expected outcome: The cart and dock are mechanically safe and visibly undamaged.

steps.title: 4. Verify External Power
steps.instructions: If the cart, dock, or monitor requires AC power: Confirm the power cord is connected Verify the outlet Check accessible power connections Confirm normal power indications where provided Expected outcome: Required accessory power is available. If restoring external power corrects the failure, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Reseat External Connections
steps.instructions: With the system safely positioned, disconnect and reconnect accessible: Docking connections External monitor video cables Cart accessory cables Power connections Do not force connectors. Expected outcome: Connections are fully seated and communication is restored.

steps.title: 6. Confirm Proper Docking or System Seating
steps.instructions: If the PX interfaces through a dock, verify it is fully positioned and latched according to normal operating use. Check that no object or cable prevents complete seating. Expected outcome: The system is mechanically and electrically engaged with the dock.

steps.title: 7. Verify External Monitor Power and Input
steps.instructions: For an external monitor: Confirm the monitor powers on Check the selected video input using normal controls Confirm the video cable is connected at both ends Inspect the cable for damage Expected outcome: The external monitor is powered, set to the correct input, and receives video from the PX.

steps.title: 8. Test a Known-Good Cable or Monitor When Available
steps.instructions: Substitute an approved known-good external display cable or compatible monitor. Do not change multiple components simultaneously if the failure can be isolated one item at a time. Expected outcome: The problem follows the cable/monitor or remains with the PX/docking interface.

steps.title: 9. Compare Docked and Standalone Operation
steps.instructions: If the system can safely operate independently of the dock, verify normal PX startup, imaging, controls, and display in standalone operation. Expected outcome: The ultrasound system itself operates normally, helping isolate the issue to the cart or dock, or the problem persists regardless of docking.

steps.title: 10. Check for Movement-Related Intermittency
steps.instructions: With no patient dependent on the system, observe the connection while the cart and cables are moved only through normal operating positions. Do not flex or stress connectors deliberately. Expected outcome: Communication remains stable. If normal movement causes repeatable loss of display or docking functions, remove the affected accessory configuration from service.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If all visible connections and accessory power are correct, restart the PX with the intended dock or display connection established as appropriate. Expected outcome: External communication initializes normally and remains stable.

steps.title: 12. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction: Verify stable system power Confirm normal imaging Check cart/dock interaction Verify the external monitor image if used Confirm normal control operation Move the cart through ordinary positioning Confirm no intermittent communication loss Expected outcome: The PX, cart/dock, and external monitor configuration operate reliably together. Troubleshooting can stop after applicable safety and functional checks.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the external monitor on the SonoSite PX cart intermittently lost the ultrasound image.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external video cable was loose at the monitor connection, while the PX display and imaging functions remained normal.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated and secured the external monitor connection, verified stable video during normal cart movement and imaging, and returned the system to service.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Freeze, Store, or Image Capture Function Not Working
description: Troubleshoots failed freeze, store, or image capture caused by controls, workflow state, storage availability, configuration, or software responsiveness.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Documentation
steps.instructions: If image capture is required for the active examination and the PX cannot reliably freeze or store images, provide an alternate verified imaging or documentation method according to clinical workflow. Do not allow missing image documentation to go unnoticed. Expected outcome: Patient care and required image documentation can continue without depending on an unreliable capture function.

steps.title: 2. Confirm Which Function Fails
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Freeze Unfreeze Still-image capture Cine or clip capture Store function Only certain exams Only certain patients Capture works but saved images cannot be found Expected outcome: The exact failed function is reproduced and separated from export or PACS transmission problems.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Relevant Control Responds
steps.instructions: Test the touchscreen, control panel, or assigned physical control used for the function. Confirm other user inputs respond normally. Expected outcome: The command itself is being accepted. If the associated control is unresponsive, troubleshoot the control interface rather than the storage function.

steps.title: 4. Confirm the System Is in an Appropriate Imaging State
steps.instructions: Verify live imaging is active when attempting freeze or capture and that no open dialog, incomplete workflow, or screen state is preventing the expected command. Expected outcome: The function works in the correct operating state or a genuine capture problem remains.

steps.title: 5. Verify Patient and Exam Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm the current study or patient workflow is properly established as required by normal operation. Avoid changing protected system configuration. Expected outcome: The image can be associated with the active examination and storage behavior is normal.

steps.title: 6. Check Available Local Storage Indicators
steps.instructions: Review user-accessible system information for indications that storage is full, unavailable, or otherwise preventing additional image capture. Do not delete patient data unless authorized and compliant with facility policy. Expected outcome: Adequate storage is available or an identified storage-capacity problem is handled through approved data-management procedures.

steps.title: 7. Remove Nonessential External Media
steps.instructions: If USB or other external storage is attached, safely remove nonessential media and retest local freeze/store operation. This separates local image capture from external export failures. Expected outcome: Local image capture functions independently of attached external media.

steps.title: 8. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If controls function but freeze/store behavior remains abnormal, perform a normal system restart when no active patient examination depends on the unit. Expected outcome: Normal freeze and capture functionality returns and remains stable.

steps.title: 9. Test a New Nonclinical Study or Approved Test Workflow
steps.instructions: Using an appropriate test workflow: Generate a test image Freeze the image Store or capture it Confirm the saved image appears where expected Return to live imaging Avoid creating inappropriate patient records. Expected outcome: Freeze, capture, storage, and retrieval work as expected.

steps.title: 10. Verify Downstream Functions Separately
steps.instructions: If local capture works but the image does not reach PACS or external storage, do not continue treating the problem as an image-capture failure. Troubleshoot DICOM/PACS or USB export separately. Expected outcome: The failure is correctly isolated to local capture, export, or network transmission.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm: Freeze and unfreeze Still-image storage Any required clip/cine capture Saved-image retrieval Normal return to live imaging Stable operation through repeated cycles Expected outcome: Required image capture functions are reliable. Troubleshooting can stop when the system performs the workflow normally.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that images on the SonoSite PX would freeze but would not save during an examination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found local storage was unavailable to the active workflow until the system was restarted, while the capture controls remained responsive.
CCR.Resolution: Performed a controlled restart, verified repeated freeze, store, and image retrieval using a test workflow, and returned the system to service.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Measurement Package or Calculation Function Error
description: Troubleshoots unavailable or incorrect measurement and calculation functions caused by exam selection, workflow, settings, inputs, configuration, or software state.

steps.title: 1. Protect Clinical Decision-Making
steps.instructions: Do not rely on measurements or calculations that appear inconsistent, unavailable, or incorrect. If the result could influence diagnosis, treatment, medication, procedure decisions, or patient management, use another verified method or ultrasound system until the issue is resolved. Expected outcome: Clinical decisions are not based on questionable measurement output.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Measurement Complaint
steps.instructions: Record: Measurement or calculation being attempted Exam type or preset Transducer used Whether the tool is missing, disabled, or produces an unexpected result Whether the problem affects one calculation or the entire measurement package Whether the issue began after a configuration or software change Expected outcome: The exact function and conditions producing the problem are identified.

steps.title: 3. Verify the Correct Exam Type and Preset
steps.instructions: Confirm the system is using the intended clinical exam or preset for the measurement being performed. Do not alter protected presets or clinical calculation definitions during troubleshooting unless authorized. Expected outcome: The expected measurement package becomes available when the correct exam configuration is selected, or the problem persists under the correct setup.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Connected Transducer and Imaging Mode
steps.instructions: Some measurement functions depend on the current probe and imaging mode. Confirm the intended compatible probe is recognized and the required imaging mode is active. Expected outcome: The appropriate measurement tools are available for the current probe and imaging context.

steps.title: 5. Confirm the Measurement Inputs Are Complete
steps.instructions: Check whether the calculation requires multiple caliper placements, traces, patient data, or other user-entered values. Review the workflow for incomplete entries without instructing clinicians on diagnostic interpretation. Expected outcome: Required inputs are present and the system performs the calculation normally.

steps.title: 6. Check Basic Patient and Exam Data
steps.instructions: Confirm the current study contains the basic information required for the intended workflow. Incorrect or missing study information may prevent a calculation or cause an inappropriate package to appear. Expected outcome: The calculation operates normally with a correctly established study.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Another Supported Measurement
steps.instructions: Using an approved test workflow or phantom where appropriate, determine whether other basic measurement tools function. Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to one measurement package or shown to affect measurement functionality more broadly.

steps.title: 8. Restart the System
steps.instructions: When clinically appropriate, close the test workflow and perform a normal controlled restart. Recreate the test under the same known conditions. Expected outcome: Measurement functionality returns and remains stable, or the failure is reproducible after restart.

steps.title: 9. Compare With a Known-Good PX Configuration When Available
steps.instructions: Where the facility has another appropriately configured SonoSite PX, compare visible exam selections and available measurement functions without copying or changing protected configuration. Expected outcome: An obvious configuration difference is identified for authorized review, or the system appears normally configured and requires escalation.

steps.title: 10. Verify Measurement Operation With a Test Object
steps.instructions: Use a suitable phantom or test object when applicable. Perform a simple known measurement and confirm the system accepts caliper placement, displays the result, and completes the expected workflow. Do not declare quantitative calibration accuracy without using an approved performance test. Expected outcome: Basic measurement functionality operates consistently.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction: Select the appropriate exam Confirm the intended measurement package is present Perform the previously failing measurement Verify required calculations complete Repeat the workflow Confirm no unexpected error or function loss occurs Expected outcome: The measurement package functions consistently. Troubleshooting can stop after applicable performance verification.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the expected calculation tools were unavailable during an examination on the SonoSite PX.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the system had been placed in a different exam preset that did not present the expected measurement package.
CCR.Resolution: Restored the appropriate user-level exam selection, verified the required measurement workflow with a test study, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the tool was missing or produced an error

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Poor Image Quality, Dropout, or Intermittent Artifact
description: Troubleshoots degraded ultrasound images, dropout, or intermittent artifact caused by probe condition, coupling, settings, connections, positioning, or environment.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Diagnostic Reliability
steps.instructions: Do not continue clinical interpretation from an image that is unreliable, significantly degraded, or intermittently missing information. Move the examination to another verified probe or ultrasound system when image quality could affect diagnosis or procedure guidance. Expected outcome: Clinical decisions are made using reliable imaging equipment.

steps.title: 2. Reproduce and Characterize the Image Problem
steps.instructions: Determine whether the reported condition is: General poor image quality A fixed dark or missing region Intermittent dropout Repeating line or band artifact Noise throughout the image Artifact only with one probe Artifact only in one room or location Artifact that changes when the cable moves Use a suitable test object or phantom when available rather than relying solely on patient imaging. Expected outcome: The artifact pattern and conditions that reproduce it are clearly identified.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Transducer and Cable
steps.instructions: Examine the: Acoustic lens Probe housing Cable Strain reliefs Connector Look for cracks, cuts, separation, dents, contamination, fluid intrusion, or cable damage. Expected outcome: The probe is physically intact. Remove the probe from service if damage could affect electrical safety, acoustic performance, or infection-control integrity.

steps.title: 4. Verify Probe Connection
steps.instructions: Confirm the transducer connector is fully and correctly seated. Inspect accessible connector surfaces for contamination or visible damage. Expected outcome: The connection is secure and image quality is stable. If reseating corrects the artifact, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 5. Verify Coupling and Test Conditions
steps.instructions: Ensure adequate ultrasound gel and appropriate transducer contact are used when reproducing the problem. When bench testing, use a suitable phantom or test target. Expected outcome: Poor coupling or test technique is ruled out as the source of image degradation.

steps.title: 6. Check Basic Imaging Controls
steps.instructions: Verify that basic user-accessible settings are reasonable for the selected transducer and test target, including items such as: Exam or preset selection Gain Depth Focus Time-gain compensation or equivalent controls Imaging mode Avoid changing protected configuration or calibration values. Expected outcome: The image improves when an inappropriate basic setting is corrected, or the artifact remains independent of normal image controls.

steps.title: 7. Compare With a Known-Good Compatible Transducer
steps.instructions: Test another known-good compatible probe on the PX under the same conditions. Expected outcome: If the known-good probe produces a normal image, the issue likely follows the original transducer. If both probes show the same artifact, continue evaluating the system or environment.

steps.title: 8. Compare the Suspect Probe on Another Compatible System
steps.instructions: If practical, test the suspect probe on another compatible verified system using comparable conditions. Expected outcome: The problem either follows the probe or remains with the original PX, providing a clear isolation point.

steps.title: 9. Evaluate Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: If the artifact is location dependent, check for nearby equipment or electrical conditions that may contribute to interference. Compare imaging in another known-good room or power source when practical. Do not defeat grounding or protective electrical systems. Expected outcome: Environmental interference is either identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 10. Check for Intermittency During Normal Cable Positioning
steps.instructions: While imaging a test object, gently position the transducer cable through normal non-stressed orientations. Do not sharply bend or intentionally stress the cable. Expected outcome: Image quality remains stable. Reproducible dropout during normal cable movement supports removal of the affected probe from service.

steps.title: 11. Perform Final Image Verification
steps.instructions: After correction: Confirm the proper probe is recognized Use a suitable phantom or test target Verify stable image appearance Check multiple basic imaging depths/settings as appropriate Confirm no intermittent artifact occurs during normal probe handling Expected outcome: Image quality is stable and clinically usable. Troubleshooting can stop when the system passes applicable imaging and functional verification.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported intermittent vertical image dropout while using the SonoSite PX.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering reproduced the dropout with one transducer and confirmed normal imaging with a known-good compatible probe.
CCR.Resolution: Removed the affected probe from service, verified stable imaging with the replacement probe, and returned the ultrasound system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether the artifact was fixed or intermittent

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - System Will Not Power On or Startup Fails
description: Troubleshoots no-power, incomplete startup, or startup failure caused by external power, battery, connection, docking, or basic operating conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Maintain Ultrasound Availability
steps.instructions: If the SonoSite PX is needed for an active procedure, examination, vascular access, or other patient care, move clinical use to another verified ultrasound system before troubleshooting. Do not continue using equipment that powers off unexpectedly, repeatedly fails startup, smells overheated, shows visible damage, or cannot be relied upon during patient care. Expected outcome: Patient care continues on reliable equipment and the affected system can be evaluated safely.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Power or Startup Complaint
steps.instructions: Ask clinical staff what occurred: No lights or display activity Powers on only when connected to AC Begins startup but does not reach the normal operating screen Shuts down during startup Failure began after moving or docking the system Failure is intermittent Attempt a normal power-on with the system removed from clinical use. Expected outcome: The reported failure is reproduced or the current operating condition is clearly established. If the system starts normally and remains stable through repeated checks, continue with final verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the System for Obvious External Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the: Power cord and AC adapter/power components accessible to Clinical Engineering System power connector Cart or dock connections Battery installation area Display and control surfaces External ports Look for bent connectors, loose plugs, contamination, liquid intrusion, impact damage, excessive heat, or unusual odor. Expected outcome: No visible condition exists that could make operation unsafe. Remove the system from service immediately if electrical, liquid, impact, or overheating damage is found.

steps.title: 4. Verify AC Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the power cord and associated power components are fully seated. Test the wall receptacle using an appropriate method or move the system to a verified known-good outlet. If the system is mounted on a cart or dock, verify that any externally accessible cart power connections are securely connected. Expected outcome: The SonoSite PX receives reliable AC power from a verified source. If normal startup returns after correcting the outlet or connection, the issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop after final verification.

steps.title: 5. Compare AC and Battery Operation
steps.instructions: With the system safely removed from patient care, compare behavior: Connected to verified AC power Operating from the installed battery, if sufficiently charged Observe whether one operating mode succeeds while the other fails. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to AC input, battery operation, or the overall system. If the system operates normally on AC but not battery, continue with battery troubleshooting rather than assuming a startup electronics failure.

steps.title: 6. Verify Battery Seating and External Condition
steps.instructions: Power the system down before disturbing the battery if required by normal safe handling. Inspect accessible battery areas for: Improper seating Damaged contacts or housing Swelling Contamination Signs of overheating Reseat only user-accessible/removable battery components in accordance with approved facility and manufacturer practices. Expected outcome: The battery is properly installed and physically acceptable. A swollen, damaged, or overheated battery requires removal from service and appropriate battery handling.

steps.title: 7. Isolate the Cart or Dock When Practical
steps.instructions: If the PX is used with a cart or dock and the configuration permits normal standalone operation, determine whether the startup problem changes when obvious external docking connections are removed and reconnected appropriately. Do not dismantle the cart or access internal power assemblies. Expected outcome: Startup behavior is either restored after correcting an external docking connection or confirmed to be independent of the cart/dock.

steps.title: 8. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential external accessories such as: USB storage External monitor connections Network cables Other externally attached peripherals Leave only the connections required for normal startup. Attempt another controlled startup. Expected outcome: The system starts without an external peripheral affecting startup. If removing a specific accessory restores normal operation, inspect or replace that accessory before reconnecting it.

steps.title: 9. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If the system partially starts but is unresponsive, perform a normal shutdown/restart using approved operating controls. Avoid repeated forced shutdowns or undocumented recovery procedures. Expected outcome: The system reaches its normal operating state and remains responsive. If startup repeatedly stalls or crashes, escalate rather than repeatedly cycling power.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After any correction: Start the system from a powered-off state Confirm stable display and controls Verify a compatible transducer is recognized Confirm basic imaging is available Check AC and battery status as appropriate Confirm no abnormal messages or unexpected shutdown occurs Expected outcome: The SonoSite PX starts normally, remains stable, and supports basic imaging functions. Troubleshooting can stop and the system may be returned to service after applicable safety and functional checks.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SonoSite PX would not power on when needed for an ultrasound examination.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the system connected through an unreliable AC power source, while the unit started normally from a verified outlet.
CCR.Resolution: Connected the system to verified AC power, completed repeated startups and basic imaging verification, and returned the unit to service.

helpfulDetails: Evidence of damage, heat, odor, or liquid exposure

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Touchscreen, Trackpad, or Control Panel Unresponsive
description: Troubleshoots unresponsive controls caused by contamination, obstruction, software state, external accessories, power conditions, or localized control failure.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient and Procedure
steps.instructions: If controls become unreliable during an active procedure or examination, discontinue dependence on the affected PX and move to another verified ultrasound system. Do not continue clinical use when the operator cannot reliably select controls, freeze images, adjust imaging, or respond to prompts. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with fully controllable equipment.

steps.title: 2. Determine Which Controls Are Affected
steps.instructions: Confirm whether the problem affects: Touchscreen only Trackpad only Specific physical controls Entire control panel All user input Controls only after prolonged use Controls only after startup or docking Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to a specific input method or confirmed to affect the entire interface.

steps.title: 3. Inspect for Contamination or Physical Obstruction
steps.instructions: Check the touchscreen and controls for: Gel Cleaning residue Moisture Adhesive material Gloves or covers interfering with operation Debris around movable controls Cracked or damaged surfaces Clean only according to approved device-compatible cleaning practices. Expected outcome: Control surfaces are clean, dry, and unobstructed. If operation returns after cleaning, continue with functional verification.

steps.title: 4. Check for Obvious Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Inspect the control panel, trackpad, touchscreen, hinges, and surrounding surfaces for impact damage or loose components. Expected outcome: No damage is present that could create unsafe or unpredictable operation. Physically damaged controls require removal from service.

steps.title: 5. Confirm the System Is Otherwise Responsive
steps.instructions: Observe whether: Imaging continues Display content updates Battery or system indicators change Other controls respond The system is fully frozen rather than only one input device failing Expected outcome: The problem is distinguished between a localized control failure and a broader system lockup.

steps.title: 6. Remove Nonessential External Accessories
steps.instructions: Disconnect nonessential USB devices, external displays, or other peripherals that might affect system behavior. Expected outcome: Controls either return to normal or the failure persists with a minimal external configuration.

steps.title: 7. Perform a Normal Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: When clinically safe, use the normal shutdown process if the interface permits it, then restart the PX. Avoid repeated forced shutdowns unless required by an approved recovery method. Expected outcome: All user controls respond normally after startup. If the failure immediately returns, continue isolation rather than repeatedly rebooting.

steps.title: 8. Compare Different Input Methods
steps.instructions: If only one interface is affected, test whether the same command can be performed through another normal input method where available. Do not use this as justification for continued clinical service if an essential control remains unreliable. Expected outcome: The fault is isolated to a particular touchscreen, trackpad, or control-panel function.

steps.title: 9. Check Basic Configuration Without Entering Restricted Menus
steps.instructions: Verify that the system is in a normal operating state and that no obvious user-level screen, dialog, lock, or mode is preventing expected control operation. Do not enter undocumented service menus or change protected settings. Expected outcome: Normal input operation is restored or a genuine control failure remains.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After correction: Navigate normal menus Select an appropriate exam Adjust basic imaging controls Freeze and unfreeze an image Use the trackpad Test touchscreen interaction Verify relevant physical controls Confirm stable operation over repeated commands Expected outcome: Controls respond consistently and correctly. Troubleshooting can stop when all essential user interfaces function normally.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SonoSite PX touchscreen did not respond reliably during setup.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found dried ultrasound gel and cleaning residue on the touchscreen surface, while the trackpad and other controls operated normally.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned and dried the touchscreen using approved practices, verified repeated touch and imaging-control operation, and returned the system to service.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Transducer Not Recognized or Probe Connection Failure
description: Troubleshoots missing transducers, intermittent probe recognition, or connection failures caused by connectors, probe damage, contamination, seating, or configuration.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care
steps.instructions: If the transducer becomes unavailable during an active examination or procedure, stop relying on the affected probe and provide another verified compatible transducer or ultrasound system. Do not continue using a probe with a damaged connector, cable, strain relief, acoustic lens, or evidence of fluid intrusion. Expected outcome: Patient care continues with reliable ultrasound equipment.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Reported Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether: The transducer is not listed The system reports no connected probe Recognition is intermittent Recognition changes when the cable is moved One probe fails while other probes work All probes fail on the same connection The problem began after cleaning, transport, or probe change Expected outcome: The failure is reproduced and isolated as closely as possible to a specific probe, connection, or system-wide condition.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Transducer Externally
steps.instructions: Inspect the entire accessible probe assembly, including: Acoustic lens Probe housing Cable Strain reliefs Connector housing Connector contacts or pins where safely visible Look for cuts, crushing, exposed conductors, cracks, contamination, bent contacts, liquid intrusion, or other damage. Expected outcome: No unsafe physical damage is present. Remove damaged transducers from service rather than continuing troubleshooting.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the System Probe Connection
steps.instructions: With the system in an appropriate safe state for connection changes, inspect the accessible transducer port for: Debris Bent or damaged contacts Liquid contamination Foreign material Physical damage Do not insert tools into the connector or attempt internal connector repair. Expected outcome: The connection area is clean, dry, and visibly undamaged.

steps.title: 5. Reconnect the Transducer Correctly
steps.instructions: Disconnect and reconnect the transducer using the normal approved connection method. Ensure the connector is fully seated and any normal locking mechanism is correctly engaged. Avoid forcing the connector. Expected outcome: The transducer is recognized and becomes available for imaging. If recognition is stable after reconnection, proceed to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Restart the System With a Minimal Configuration
steps.instructions: If the probe remains unrecognized, perform a normal controlled system restart. Reconnect only the required transducer and avoid unnecessary peripherals during the test. Expected outcome: The system starts normally and recognizes the probe. If not, continue with substitution testing.

steps.title: 7. Test a Known-Good Compatible Transducer
steps.instructions: Connect an approved known-good compatible transducer to the same available system connection. Do not substitute an incompatible probe. Expected outcome: If the known-good probe is recognized, the original probe or its cable/connector is the likely source. If neither probe is recognized, investigate the system connection or broader configuration.

steps.title: 8. Test the Suspect Probe on Another Compatible System When Available
steps.instructions: If facility resources permit, connect the suspect probe to another compatible verified SonoSite system or appropriate test configuration. Expected outcome: The comparison confirms whether the problem follows the transducer or remains with the original PX system.

steps.title: 9. Check Basic Probe Selection and System Configuration
steps.instructions: Confirm that the system is operating in an appropriate mode and that the connected transducer is normally supported by the configured system. Do not enter unauthorized service menus or make undocumented configuration changes. Expected outcome: No basic selection or configuration condition is preventing recognition.

steps.title: 10. Verify Imaging After Recognition Is Restored
steps.instructions: Once the probe is recognized: Confirm the correct probe identification Generate an image on an appropriate test object or phantom Gently position the cable through normal ranges without stressing it Watch for intermittent disconnects or image dropout Expected outcome: Probe recognition and imaging remain stable. Troubleshooting can stop when the connection is reliable and the probe passes applicable functional inspection.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SonoSite PX intermittently failed to recognize the connected ultrasound transducer.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the transducer connector was not fully seated, while the probe and system connector showed no visible damage.
CCR.Resolution: Reconnected and secured the transducer, verified stable recognition and imaging through repeated checks, and returned the system to service.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or all probes were affected
Suspect probe result on another system
Whether cable movement reproduced the failure

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - USB Export or External Storage Failure
description: Troubleshoots failed USB export or external storage caused by media compatibility, connection, file workflow, device condition, storage capacity, or port problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Data
steps.instructions: Do not delete locally stored patient images simply because export has failed. Follow facility privacy, cybersecurity, and approved removable-media policies when using external storage. Expected outcome: Patient data remains preserved and only approved storage media is used.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Export Complaint
steps.instructions: Determine whether: USB device is not recognized Export begins but fails Export completes but files are absent Only certain studies fail One USB device fails while another works All external storage devices fail The USB port is physically loose or damaged Expected outcome: The problem is clearly defined as media recognition, export workflow, file creation, or physical connection failure.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the USB Port and External Media
steps.instructions: Inspect externally without inserting tools. Look for: Bent or damaged port structure Debris Liquid contamination Loose connector fit Cracked USB device Damaged connector Expected outcome: The port and media are visibly intact and safe to use. Physical damage requires removal from service or escalation as appropriate.

steps.title: 4. Verify the Media Is Approved for Use
steps.instructions: Confirm the USB device meets facility cybersecurity and device-use requirements. Avoid unknown, personal, or unapproved removable media. Expected outcome: An approved external storage device is used for testing.

steps.title: 5. Reconnect the USB Device
steps.instructions: Remove and reconnect the media using the normal USB interface. Allow the system time to detect the device before attempting export. Expected outcome: The storage device is recognized. If recognition returns and export works, continue to final verification.

steps.title: 6. Check External Storage Capacity
steps.instructions: If user-accessible information is available, determine whether the external storage device has sufficient available capacity. Do not delete existing data unless authorized. Expected outcome: Adequate storage exists for the intended export.

steps.title: 7. Test With a Known-Good Approved USB Device
steps.instructions: Use a known-good approved device with available capacity. Expected outcome: If the known-good media works, the original USB device is the likely cause. If neither works, continue evaluating the PX port and workflow.

steps.title: 8. Verify Local Image Storage First
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended images or study exist locally on the PX before troubleshooting export. Expected outcome: The source data is present and available for export. Missing local images indicate a capture/storage issue rather than USB export failure.

steps.title: 9. Verify the Correct Export Workflow
steps.instructions: Confirm the intended study or images are selected and the normal export destination is chosen. Do not change protected data-management configuration. Expected outcome: The system initiates the export to the selected external storage device.

steps.title: 10. Test Another Accessible USB Port if Applicable
steps.instructions: If the PX configuration provides another approved accessible USB interface intended for storage, compare behavior. Expected outcome: The failure is isolated to one external connection or shown to affect USB storage generally.

steps.title: 11. Perform a Controlled Restart
steps.instructions: If media and workflow are correct but recognition remains abnormal, safely remove the USB device and restart the system. Reconnect approved media after normal startup. Expected outcome: The device is recognized and export succeeds.

steps.title: 12. Verify the Exported Data
steps.instructions: After a successful export: Confirm export completes without error Safely remove the storage device according to the normal workflow Verify the expected files are present using an approved facility computer or workflow when permitted Protect patient information throughout verification Expected outcome: The expected data is successfully exported and retrievable. Troubleshooting can stop once reliable export is confirmed.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SonoSite PX would not recognize the USB drive used for approved image export.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the original USB device was not recognized, while a known-good approved USB device was detected and exported normally.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced the failed external storage media, verified export and retrieval of a test study, and returned the system to service.

title: Fujifilm Sonosite PX Ultrasound System - Wi-Fi, DICOM, PACS, or Worklist Failure
description: Troubleshoots failed network connection, worklist retrieval, or image transmission caused by connectivity, configuration, destination availability, or infrastructure.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Care and Preserve Images
steps.instructions: If network functions fail during clinical use, ensure images remain locally available and follow the facility's approved downtime or alternate documentation workflow. Do not delete studies or repeatedly modify network settings while trying to restore transmission. Expected outcome: Patient imaging data is preserved and clinical workflow can continue safely.

steps.title: 2. Identify Which Network Function Failed
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem involves: Wi-Fi connection Wired LAN connection Worklist retrieval DICOM image transmission PACS destination All network functions One destination only One room or wireless location only Expected outcome: The failure is narrowed to network access, worklist, transmission, or a specific destination.

steps.title: 3. Confirm the Ultrasound System Otherwise Operates Normally
steps.instructions: Verify: Normal startup Imaging functionality Local image storage Controls Patient study creation Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to communications rather than a broader system malfunction.

steps.title: 4. Check Physical Network Connections When Wired
steps.instructions: For wired operation: Inspect the network cable Confirm connectors are fully seated Check the wall jack or network connection Substitute a known-good approved cable when available Observe normal user-accessible connection indicators if present Expected outcome: A secure physical network path exists. If replacing or reseating the cable restores communication, continue to end-to-end verification.

steps.title: 5. Check Wi-Fi Connection Status
steps.instructions: For wireless operation, verify the PX shows connection to the intended facility wireless network through normal user-accessible status information. Compare behavior in another known-good wireless area if the failure appears location dependent. Do not create unauthorized hotspots or connect patient equipment to unapproved networks. Expected outcome: The system connects to the intended approved network or the failure is isolated to wireless access.

steps.title: 6. Verify Basic Network Configuration
steps.instructions: Review authorized user-accessible network information and compare it with the facility's documented configuration. Check for obvious issues involving: Network selection IP addressing method Addressing information Gateway DICOM destination Worklist destination Do not guess values or change production configuration without approved information. Expected outcome: The system configuration matches the approved network design or a discrepancy is identified for correction by authorized personnel.

steps.title: 7. Determine Whether Other Devices Are Affected
steps.instructions: Check with clinical users or appropriate IT/PACS personnel to determine whether: Other ultrasound systems can retrieve worklists Other modalities can send to the same PACS The affected location has a broader network outage The DICOM or worklist destination is available Expected outcome: The problem is isolated to the PX or identified as an infrastructure/service issue.

steps.title: 8. Test Worklist and Transmission Separately
steps.instructions: If possible: Attempt worklist retrieval Acquire and locally store a nonclinical test image according to facility practice Send the test image to the configured destination Expected outcome: The specific failing communication path is identified rather than assuming all DICOM functions are down.

steps.title: 9. Verify Destination and Study Selection
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct configured destination is selected and the intended study is queued or selected appropriately for transmission. Do not resend large numbers of patient studies indiscriminately. Expected outcome: The intended image is sent to the correct destination without duplication.

steps.title: 10. Perform a Controlled Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: After confirming infrastructure and configuration, perform a normal restart of the PX when it is not supporting active patient care. Expected outcome: Network services reconnect normally and remain available.

steps.title: 11. Confirm End-to-End Communication
steps.instructions: After correction: Verify network connection Retrieve the worklist if applicable Send a controlled test image Confirm receipt at the intended PACS or receiving system Confirm no unintended duplicate or wrong-destination transmission Expected outcome: The complete communication path works from the PX to the intended destination. Troubleshooting can stop when end-to-end operation is verified.

CCR.Complaint: Clinical staff reported that the SonoSite PX could image patients but could not send studies to PACS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the external network cable connection was loose, while local image storage and system operation were normal.
CCR.Resolution: Reseated the network connection, sent a controlled test image, confirmed receipt at PACS, and returned the system to normal service.
